quotes.name: Vinnie Keane
quotes.quote: The A's are a big part of Oakland's identity, and I'm proud to have been a part of it. I feel like they bring the community together, especially on game days. I've seen it firsthand in Grand Lake, where people come out to support the team. It's not just about the games, though - the A's have a presence in the city that's hard to ignore. I've been recognized a couple of times at the grocery store recently, and it's nice to feel like I'm still a part of something bigger than myself. As for their influence on the community, I think it's positive overall. They've got a lot of young talent coming up, and it's exciting to see what the future holds.

quotes.name: Henry Rivas
quotes.quote: The A's are a big part of my life, and I plan my days around the games. When I'm not pitching, I'm thinking about the next start or recovering from the last one. I've lived in West Oakland for a while now, and I see the neighborhood changing. More people are moving in, and it's getting livelier. I think the A's bring a sense of community and pride to the area. I'm proud to be a part of it, and I hope we can keep being a positive presence here.

quotes.name: Kai Tanaka
quotes.quote: To be honest, I haven't really thought much about The A's and their community engagement in West Oakland. I live in Fruitvale, and while I'm aware of the team, it's not something that's directly impacted my daily life. I mean, I know they're based in Oakland, but my connection to them is pretty casual. I do notice when there's a lot of activity around the city, and sometimes I hear conversations about the team, but it's not something I engage with regularly.

quotes.name: Evan Lewis
quotes.quote: To be honest, I haven't really seen much of The A's around West Oakland lately. I drive past the Coliseum all the time, and you can tell when there's a game or event going on, but it's not like they're out in the community that much. I mean, I've seen Arturo Ramos and John Ellis around Laurel, they're nice guys, but that's about it. I'm not sure how much they're really engaging with the community in West Oakland.
